Commentary.Commentary: Right then, that’s all from this entertaining encounter as West Indies take a 1-0 lead in the series. They’ll be eager to wrap it up in the next game, while Bangladesh will fight hard to take it to a decider. The second T20I will be played right here on the 29th of October, Wednesday, starting at 12 pm GMT. As always, do join us a bit earlier for all the pre-match build-up and excitement. Until then, take care and goodbye!

Shai Hope, the victorious skipper of West Indies, says that they assessed the conditions better but still feels that they could have scored more runs and goes on to applaud the way Rovman Powell batted. Adds that when the players come out and execute their individual plans, it becomes easier as a captain to set the field and make decisions.

Rovman Powell is the PLAYER OF THE MATCH for his fantastic knock in his 100th T20I. He says that he was very pleased at the end of his innings. Adds that at one point he was 7 off 20 balls but backed himself and believed that one big shot could change the momentum. Mentions that he and Hope were constantly having conversations about when to take on the bowlers, and it worked out in the death overs. Ends by saying that if they could have got hold of a few more, they could have scored more runs.

Litton Das, the captain of Bangladesh, says that West Indies batted really well in the first 10 overs but feels that till the 19th over, they were ahead in the game, and the game changed in just one over, which happens in cricket. Adds that they lost too many wickets in the Powerplay and reckons that Shamim Hossain also needed to take more responsibility and show more experience. Mentions that the opposition took a couple of brilliant catches as well, which makes a difference.
Presentation Time...

West Indies will be delighted with their all-round bowling performance. Akeal Hosein was taken on early but bounced back strongly after a stunning catch from Romario Shepherd set the tone. Akeal struck twice in the Powerplay, while Jason Holder and Jayden Seales added one each to put Bangladesh on the back foot. Khary Pierre joined the act soon after, and the visitors had half the side back in the hut within 10 overs. There was a brief fightback from the hosts, but as the required rate climbed, the bowlers tightened things up again. Seales and Holder finished with three wickets apiece, and Romario Shepherd wrapped things up. West Indies’ fielding, especially their catching, was simply outstanding. In fact, a few of those grabs could easily be contenders for catch of the season in any league.

Earlier in the game, West Indies posted a solid total on the board, though runs didn’t come easily early on. The openers laid a steady foundation with 35 runs in the Powerplay, both going on to contribute in the 30s. The real momentum came from an 83-run stand between Rovman Powell and Shai Hope. Playing his 100th T20I, Powell had a scratchy start and even got a reprieve, but once set, he was unstoppable - finishing unbeaten on 44 off 28 balls with four towering sixes. The duo smashed 51 runs in the final three overs to lift the total past 160. For Bangladesh, Taskin Ahmed and Rishad Hossain picked up wickets but were expensive, while Fizz and Nasum Ahmed kept things tight before the death overs undid their good work.

At the start of the chase, Bangladesh seemed set for a smooth ride - the ball was coming on nicely, dew was setting in, and chasing sides had done well at this venue. But things quickly went downhill after Tanzid Hasan departed following a few crisp shots, perhaps playing one stroke too many. From there, the innings unraveled rapidly - slipping to 41/4 and later 77/6. Just when it looked over, Tanzim Hasan Sakib and Nasum Ahmed launched a spirited counterattack, finding a couple of big overs to spark some hope. However, both fell at crucial moments for 33 and 20, respectively, leaving too much for the tail to do. Maybe sending Rishad Hossain earlier could’ve changed the script, but in the end, it was a mountain too high for the hosts..

West Indies draw first blood in this three-match T20I series with a commanding all-round performance. After being second-best in two of the three ODIs, the visitors have bounced back in style to make a strong statement. Former skipper, Rovman Powell, playing his 100th T20I, led from the front with a decisive knock, which included 3 massive sixes in the last over that turned the game in their favour. Bangladesh, on the other hand, will have plenty to think about, especially their batting, which never quite found its rhythm in the chase.

OUT! HIT WICKET! What a bizarre way to get out! Taskin Ahmed has literally nailed a pull shot and sent the ball into the stands but he's gone too far back in the crease and has ended up getting his heel on the stumps and one of the bails has come off. Coming to the delivery, this is dug in short and around off by Romario Shepherd. Taskin is ready for it and looks to pull it from deep inside the crease and he gets plenty on it as well but unfortunately, that will be the end of his inning and also of this match. Bangladesh get bowled out for 149 and West Indies win by 16 runs!

The floodlight tower is malfunctioning once again, and the umpires have taken this opportunity to call for DRINKS. West Indies have dominated proceedings so far in this chase, picking up 5 wickets and not giving away many runs as well. The bowlers have worked in tandem and have not let any batter settle in after that expensive first over. The Windies will look to continue like this and quickly wrap things up, and not let this game drag deep. Bangladesh, on the other hand, are in desperate need of a partnership. Tawhid Hridoy has looked good, but he will need support from others. Tanzim Hasan Sakib has been sent ahead of Rishad Hossain, probably to give him the freedom to play some shots and try to change the momentum. Let's see if it works out or not for them here.

Commentary.Commentary: Shorter in length and over middle, pulled away just in front of mid-wicket for a single.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 6.5: Romario Shepherd to Tawhid Hridoy, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Hridoy charges down the track and Romario sees him coming. Bowls it a bit short and right at the batter. Hridoy gets cramped up and has to just dab it down to point.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 6.4: Romario Shepherd to Tawhid Hridoy, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Full of a good length, angled in towards off, Hridoy plants his front leg across but the ball skids on and nearly goes through the defences.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 6.3: Romario Shepherd to Tawhid Hridoy, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Full and angled into the legs, flicked away past square leg for one more.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 6.2: Romario Shepherd to Nurul Hasan, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Hard-length delivery, on the pads, clipped away towards deep mid-wicket for a single by Hridoy.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 6.1: Romario Shepherd to Tawhid Hridoy, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Change? Yes, Romario Shepherd replaces Akeal Hosein. At this stage, West Indies were 35/0, while Bangladesh are 42/4. The hosts are ahead on the runs but have lost way too many wickets.
Holder goes wider on the crease and spears the ball in towards the wickets, Nurul Hasan gets inside the line and blocks it with a straight bat.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 5.6: Jason Holder to Nurul Hasan, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Nagging length darted in towards the stumps, Nurul ets a bit squared up but keeps it out.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 5.5: Jason Holder to Nurul Hasan, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Edged but doesn't carry! Beautiful seam position from Holder, serving it on a tad fuller length in the channel and getting it to nip away. Nurul Hasan pushes at it with soft hands and edges it short of the first slip fielder.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 5.4: Jason Holder to Nurul Hasan, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Wide! Bowls this one full and pushes it down the leg side for a wide.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 5.4: Jason Holder to Nurul Hasan, Wide!

Commentary.Commentary: Nurul Hasan walks out to bat now. A slip in place now as well.

OUT! BOWLED'EM! Jason Holder gets a wicket in his first over and things go from bad to worse for Bangladesh. Holder shaves off a few clicks from the delivery and serves it on a good length on off and middle. The ball naturally slants away and Shamim Hossain has a swipe across the line. But, Shamim is through the shot early and the ball goes on to knock over the top of off stump.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 5.3: Jason Holder to Shamim Hossain, OUT! b Jason Holder.

Commentary.Commentary: Hard length on leg, nudged away to mid-wicket by Shamim Hossain.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 5.2: Jason Holder to Shamim Hossain, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Starts back of a length and slants it into the batter, Tawhid Hridoy tucks it down through backward square leg for a single.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 5.1: Jason Holder to Tawhid Hridoy, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Flighted, full and on leg, Tawhid Hridoy flicks it through mid-wicket for one.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 4.6: Akeal Hosein to Tawhid Hridoy, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Drags his length back, on off, Tawhid Hridoy punches it to the left of the bowler. Akeal Hosein grabs it and gives a stare to the batter.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 4.5: Akeal Hosein to Tawhid Hridoy, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Darts this one full and on leg, Shamim Hossain clips it through square leg for a run.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 4.4: Akeal Hosein to Shamim Hossain, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Quicker, short and on middle, Shamim Hossain pats it towards mid on.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 4.3: Akeal Hosein to Shamim Hossain, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Shamim Hossain is in at number 5.

OUT! TAKEN! Akeal Hosein gets his second in the Powerplay! He bowls this flatter, fuller and on middle and leg. Saif Hassan goes down to swipe it away but gets it more from the inner half of the bat. It goes quickly towards short fine leg, where Romario Shepherd gets taken aback a bit by how quickly it came at him, but takes a good catch. Hassan walks back for 8 off 7, and Bangladesh are three down now.
Commentary.Howout: c Romario Shepherd b Akeal Hosein
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 4.2: Akeal Hosein to Saif Hassan, OUT! c Romario Shepherd b Akeal Hosein.

Commentary.Commentary: Short and on middle, Tawhid Hridoy nudges it through mid-wicket for a single.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 4.1: Akeal Hosein to Tawhid Hridoy, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Tossed up, full and on leg, Tawhid Hridoy tucks it to short fine for one.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.6: Khary Pierre to Tawhid Hridoy, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Fires one full and on leg, angling in. Tawhid Hridoy stays back to work it away but misses and gets hit on the pads.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.5: Khary Pierre to Tawhid Hridoy, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Floated, full and on middle, Tawhid Hridoy uses his feet and clips it towards deep square leg for a brace.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.4: Khary Pierre to Tawhid Hridoy, 2 runs.

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR! Good shot! Flatter, short and outside off, Tawhid Hridoy waits for it and cuts it late through backward point. It teases the fielder all the way but wins the race to the fence for a boundary.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.3: Khary Pierre to Tawhid Hridoy, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: Shortish and on leg, Saif Hassan clips it towards square leg for a single.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.2: Khary Pierre to Saif Hassan, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Sees the batter advance and drags his length back, on middle, Saif Hassan looks to work it away but mises and gets hit on the pads.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.1: Khary Pierre to Saif Hassan, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Flighted, full and on middle, Tawhid Hridoy blocks it out.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.6: Akeal Hosein to Tawhid Hridoy, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Tawhid Hridoy is the next batter in.

OUT! CAUGHT AND BOWLED! Another screamer of a catch! Akeal Hosein tosses it up, shortish and on middle, sticks to the surface a bit. Litton Das stays back, looks to punch it toward long on but just checks his shot and ends up lobbing it wide of the bowler. Hosein, in his follow-through, moves to his right. He has to go around the non-striker and just sticks his right hand out. The ball gets stuck in and Litton is absolutely stunned at the crease. Bangladesh are 29/2, chasing 166 runs!
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.5: Akeal Hosein to Litton Das, OUT! c & b Akeal Hosein.

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR! Nice shot! Flatter, full and on middle and off, Litton Das goes down and plays the reverse sweep over the short third fielder for a boundary.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.4: Akeal Hosein to Litton Das, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: RIPPER! Slows it up, full and around off, grips and turns away sharply, Litton Das gets drawn forwad to push it away but gets beaten on the outside edge.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.3: Akeal Hosein to Litton Das, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Flatter, full but down the leg side, Litton Das goes down to paddle it away but misses. Shai Hope, the keeper also only manages to parry it behind towards the third man region. Two byes taken. If you are wondering why it is not called a wide, it is because according to the new ICC rules, there is an extra guideline to give some more leniency to the bowler, and this ball was inside that line.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.2: Akeal Hosein to Litton Das, 2 Byes.

Commentary.Commentary: Floated, short and around off, turns away, Litton Das backs away and steers it towards cover-point.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.1: Akeal Hosein to Litton Das, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: SIX! BOOM! Saif Hassan joins the party now! Short of a length and around middle, sits up nicely for the batter. Hassan picks up the length early, swivels and pulls it with disdain over the deep square leg fence for a biggie. 11 runs and a wicket from the over!
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.6: Jayden Seales to Saif Hassan, Six!

Commentary.Commentary: Touch fuller and on middle and off, Litton Das taps it just wide of covers for a single and gets off the mark.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.5: Jayden Seales to Litton Das, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: On a length and on off, Litton Das pushes it to covers.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.4: Jayden Seales to Litton Das, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Good length and on middle, Litton Das blocks it out.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.3: Jayden Seales to Litton Das, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Skipper, Litton Das walks in at number 3 for Bangladesh.

OUT! TAKEN! Oh...wow! That is an absolute STUNNER! Jayden Seales bangs this into the pitch, on middle and off. Tanzid Hasan tries to flat-bat it over the bowler's head but the ball just gets big on him and he mistimes it over mid on. Romario Shepherd runs backwards, flings himself, and tries to grab it with his extended arms. The ball gets stuck on his right hand and he does well to hold onto it even after a big impact with the ground. Gets a hug from Jason Holder and the Windies are fired up with that. Hasan walks back for 15 off 5, and Bangladesh are 16/1!
Commentary.Howout: c Romario Shepherd b Jayden Seales
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.2: Jayden Seales to Tanzid Hasan, OUT! c Romario Shepherd b Jayden Seales.

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR! Welcome to the game, Jayden Seales! Back of a length and just outside off. Tanzid Hasan skips down the track, extends his arms and slaps it through extra covers for a cracking boundary.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.1: Jayden Seales to Tanzid Hasan, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: Jayden Seales will share the new ball with Akeal Hosein.
Another short delivery, on off, Saif Hassan stays back and blocks it out. 12 runs off the first over then!
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.6: Akeal Hosein to Saif Hassan, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Slows it up, shortish and around off, turns in, Tanzid Hasan stays back and works it towards long on for a run.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.5: Akeal Hosein to Tanzid Hasan, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR! Put away! Dragged back and on middle, Tanzid Hasan rocks back quickly, gets on top of it and smashes it over the leaping mid-wicket fielder for a boundary now.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.4: Akeal Hosein to Tanzid Hasan, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: SIX! BANG! Poor delivery and gets the right treatment! Akeal Hosein goes short and down the leg side, begging to be put away. Tanzid Hasan gets on one knee and whacks it over the deep square leg fence for the first biggie of the chase.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.3: Akeal Hosein to Tanzid Hasan, Six!

Commentary.Commentary: Bangladesh get underway in the chase! The arm ball now, full and on middle, drifts in sharply. Saif Hassan gets a bit hurried but manages to knock it towards mid on for a single.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.2: Akeal Hosein to Saif Hassan, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Some turn! Akeal Hosein starts with a floater, short and on middle, turning it away sharply. Saif Hassan stays back and pats it towards short covers.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.1: Akeal Hosein to Saif Hassan, No run.
